name: Methyldiazinol

lead: Methyldiazinol is an oral steroid made in the 1960s as a modified version of mestanolone. The appearance payoff people associate with it is more muscle mass.

It is a 17α-methylated DHT analogue, so it is presumed to work by activating the androgen receptor. An old animal measurement reported a muscle-to-androgenic ratio of 15 relative to oral methyltestosterone, among the highest in the early literature. It was never marketed, and no human studies have been published.

paras: There is no established practical use. It was never sold as a drug, and it appears only in the 1965 chemistry paper and in later descriptions of that work, so there is no routine, form or timeline to describe.

No human safety data exist and it has no approved use. As a 17α-methylated oral androgen, it belongs to a class associated with liver strain and androgenic side effects, but its own effects in people have not been described.

angle.text: The interest in methyldiazinol is muscle gain: it is a DHT-type steroid that reportedly activated androgen receptors strongly relative to its androgenic effect in animals. That 1965 animal measurement is the whole basis for the idea, and it was never marketed or tested in people.

lead: Methyldiazinol (3,3-azo-17α-methyl-5α-dihydrotestosterone, or 3-azi-17α-methyl-DHT) is a synthetic, orally active androgen and anabolic steroid that was never marketed.[1] Its interest for muscle and physique comes from a historical animal finding: it showed a high ratio of muscle-building (myotrophic) to androgenic activity, reported as 15 relative to oral methyltestosterone, among the highest observed in the old literature.[1]

Chemically it is a 17α-methyl derivative of dihydrotestosterone, specifically the 3-azi (diazirine) analogue of mestanolone (17α-methyl-DHT).[1] It was described in a 1965 paper by Church, Kende and Weiss in the Journal of the American Chemical Society on steroid diaziridines and diazirines.[1]
Only that early animal-era data and chemistry exist; no human studies have been published.

paras: Methyldiazinol is the C3 azi (3,3-azo) analogue of mestanolone and a 17α-methylated derivative of DHT, with formula C20H32N2O and a molar mass of about 316.5 g/mol.[1]

The only available pharmacology is a historical animal bioassay ratio of myotrophic to androgenic activity, reported as about 15 (3 to 0.2) relative to methyltestosterone.[1] Wikipedia cites Kochakian's 2012 book Anabolic-Androgenic Steroids as reporting this dissociation, which traces back to the 1965 chemistry paper.[1] Mechanism and human pharmacokinetics have not been described.[1]

timeline.event: Described by Church, Kende and Weiss in the Journal of the American Chemical Society.[1]
